capabilities.local_comparison: Compare two local controller solves at the same saved state/previous input/horizon with exactly one adopted weight change. Measures local plan/endpoint differences; does not establish closed-loop settling or causal attribution. Requires a saved effective horizon matching the authorized horizon.
capabilities.prediction_braking: At one saved projected state, compare recorded input with instantaneous braking-box input over the fixed short horizon. Can measure local endpoint speed/position differences. Cannot separate objective weighting, seed selection, horizon effects or backend-model mismatch when they predict the same result; cannot identify the dominant settling cause.

design_response_content.reasoning: Disposition "defer": I concur that no control-parameter change is warranted yet — the handed-over report leaves every candidate cause of the settling failure unresolved and rules out only one mechanism. Evidence basis (world-tip vectors; projected GVS state). Reach passed while sampled settling failed: terminal tip error 0.00764 m [fea26b997f974] is within the 0.01 m reach tolerance with reach_passed true [f9105d17871c6], yet settled tipping failed — late-window max error 0.058 m [f8e7ac55fafdc] exceeds the 0.01 m settling position limit [f987135c25ec9], and terminal speed 0.635 m/s [fc93fb8a18b10] and late max speed 1.581 m/s [f9c4843fbdf6e] exceed the 0.02 m/s speed limit [f939cd53125f8]. Open candidates: solver stop-short (34 "User_Requested_Stop" [fc3ee64814ec6] vs 1 "Solve_Succeeded" [fb93c52be0a9f], all plans still accepted), shrinking lookahead (effective horizon 8 [fe5fc6ea35ca2] to 3 [f9b529db84686] control intervals), projected-GVS vs backend endpoint differences (matched tip differences ~0.006–0.008 m [fc08e788d9252, f955f44ca11ab]), and weak velocity/terminal weighting. Ruled out: wall-clock overrun — 35 deadline misses [f90f1ab1c0b4d] with mean update 17.08 s [ff3c306d596b0] cannot inject physical delay under synchronous fixed-step scheduling. The single authorized bounded 0.01 s saved-state check (model.gvs@1.0.0, implicit_euler, step 0.002 s; local_solves<=6, prediction_evaluations<=24) has not been executed in this phase, so its local endpoint speed/position difference is not yet measured. Next action "request_check" to run that one bounded check at a single saved projected state; a 0.01 s projected-model probe and single-execution comparisons cannot establish a dominant cause. Deferring the recommendation executes nothing by itself.

instructions: Select one discriminating check based on unresolved hypotheses. Inspect retained evidence as needed to choose the operation and update_id. The host binds the chosen update's exact measured_initial_state and operation-defined input from the inventory controller file; do not copy vectors. prediction_braking uses current actual_tension_n; local_comparison uses previous actual_tension_n and requires the exact adopted parameter/value and a saved effective plan horizon of 0.01 s. prediction_braking compares held recorded input with an instantaneous braking box solution and requires no adoption. Choose update_id >= 1, hypotheses, fixed conditions, metrics, acceptance criteria and work_limits (wall_s <= 300; prediction_evaluations=2 or local_solves=2). Host fixes model.gvs@1.0.0, implicit Euler, 0.002 s step and 0.01 s horizon. At most two successful reading turns, then select the check. Do not overextend a local probe to the entire settling failure. State local_question, competing hypotheses, discriminating_observations and unresolved questions. If hypotheses predict the same result, explicitly say this check cannot separate them. Select a question the stated capability can answer; no dominant-cause claim. Availability status applies to the entire inventory entry unless you supply update_ids (controller updates) or time_range_s (sampled backend motion). For a partially read entry, use queried and describe missing coverage, or explicitly scope a not_read/not_displayed declaration to the unread subset.

recommendations.rationale: Retained evidence is consistent with several unresolved causes (residual tip speed under weak velocity weighting, solver stop-short, shrinking effective horizon, projected-model mismatch) and does not distinguish them; defer any control-parameter change until the single authorized bounded 0.01 s saved-state check is executed.

attribution.reason: Terminal and late tip speeds greatly exceed the 0.02 m/s settling limit while terminal position is within tolerance; the saved objective weights velocity terms small (velocity_weight 0.0001, terminal_velocity_weight 0.0001, terminal_tip_speed_weight 0.0, holding_tip_speed_weight 0.0) with terminal_weight 5.0. Raw weight magnitudes do not establish cost-term importance without actual contributions/scaling, so this stays unresolved.

34 of 35 selections are 'User_Requested_Stop' against 1 'Solve_Succeeded', with policy_stop_reason 'budget_best_feasible' or 'relative_seed_improvement'; plans were still 'plan_accepted' true. A stop-short category does not by itself establish suboptimality or its link to settling, and no iteration traces are retained.

Effective horizon declines from 8 to 3 control intervals across the sampled late updates (far below the configured horizon of 10). A reduced lookahead could limit braking/terminal-speed shaping, but the retained signals do not separate horizon from solver stops or weighting.

Projected-GVS predictions and recorded serial-backend endpoints differ by small but nonzero world-tip distances and one-step velocity-vector norms. Boxed 0.01 s comparisons cannot establish that this mismatch dominates settling, so it remains a candidate.

35 deadline misses and mean_update_s 17.075238151415917 s versus a 0.01 s control period are recorded, but scheduling is synchronous: controller calls complete before fixed-count backend steps and wall deadline misses do not inject physical delay into simulated time, so a wall-clock mechanism cannot directly cause the physical settling failure.

At update 30 the applied/requested tension on channel 0 is 7.990411884680996 N, close to the 8.0 N per-tendon limit held in source.force_limits; force-limit proximity could bound available braking tension, but the retained signals do not quantify lost authority, so this is unresolved.

facts.statement: Reach passed while sampled settling failed: terminal tip error 0.007642608585867386 m is within the 0.01 m reach tolerance and reach_passed is true, but sampled_settling_passed is false, with late-window max tip error 0.05813810428573256 m against the 0.01 m settling position limit.
Tip speed is far above the settling limit: terminal tip speed 0.6351726092425104 m/s and late-window max speed 1.5810152739742807 m/s both exceed the 0.02 m/s settling_criteria speed limit.

Late-window selections ended short of convergence with shrinking lookahead: effective horizon falls from 8 control intervals at update 27 to 3 at update 32, only 1 of 35 selections reports 'Solve_Succeeded' versus 34 'User_Requested_Stop', and the run logs 35 deadline misses with mean_update_s 17.075238151415917 s against a 0.01 s control period.

Projected-GVS versus recorded-backend comparisons at updates 27 to 29 show small but nonzero world-tip differences of 0.0059230819406683064 m (update 27) and 0.0076898869753466255 m (update 29) and one-step velocity-vector difference norms of 0.021386880777076088 m/s (update 28) and 0.14969247760063253 m/s (update 29).

limitations: No historical optimizer iterations or full warm plans are reconstructed; source.historical_full_plans is not retained.
Single execution and model comparisons do not establish a dominant cause.
Full sampled backend q/qdot are retained, but the motion view displays only the final settling window and no closed-loop counterfactual replay exists.

Projected states are projected GVS coordinates, not full backend-state error.

Do not change control parameters based on this phase; keep weighting, solver-stop, horizon, and model-mismatch hypotheses open.

request_content.question: Why did this run fail the settling criterion while terminal reach passed? Observed in the handed-over common summary: terminal_error_m = 0.00764 m is within the 0.01 m reach tolerance and reach_passed = true, but sampled_settling_passed = false, with terminal_speed_m_s = 0.635 and late_max_speed_m_s = 1.581 against the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit and late_max_error_m = 0.058 m against the 0.01 m position limit over the 0.05 s settling window. The same run records stopping_counts = {User_Requested_Stop: 34, Solve_Succeeded: 1}, deadline_misses = 35, and mean_update_s = 17.08 s versus a 0.01 s control period; initialization_selected = 29, noninitialization_selected = 6. Which candidate explanations of the settling failure are and are not supported by the retained inventory (one-step predictions, applied tensions, saved projected states, plan selection, solver status, per-update effective horizon, tendon force limits, and the sampled backend motion view), and what bounded local endpoint speed/position difference does a single authorized short-horizon check reveal at one saved projected state? Keep all hypotheses open — e.g. terminal/velocity/weighting effects, solver non-convergence (34 non-Solve_Succeeded selections), horizon, and backend-model mismatch are candidates to be distinguished or left unresolved, not assumed.
scope: Read the complete retained inventory already itemized in the handed-over inventory: source.one_step_predictions, source.applied_tensions, source.saved_projected_states, source.plan_selection, source.solver_status, and source.controller_horizon (all record_count 35, updates 0..34), plus source.force_limits; report only what these retained signals state, with stated coverage, in world-frame tip vectors and projected GVS state coordinates.

For source.backend_motion, use the derived motion view (raw gzip bytes are not JSON-readable via evidence.read) and, if needed, matched prediction endpoint samples (at most 8 chosen controller update ids per query) to read measured backend position/velocity at the matched next timestamp; the final settling window is what motion displays.

At exactly one saved projected state, execute at most one authorized saved-state numerical check (prediction_braking and/or local_comparison) strictly within the frozen grant: model.gvs@1.0.0, implicit_euler, horizon_s 0.01, integration_step_s 0.002, max_checks 1, max_wall_s 300, local_solves<=6, prediction_evaluations<=24 — solely to measure the local endpoint speed/position difference at that state.

Excluded: production changes or backend execution; closed-loop counterfactual replay; full historical warm plans or optimizer iteration traces (source.historical_full_plans is not retained); and any claim of a dominant or settled root cause.
stopping_conditions: Stop when the answer states what the retained evidence does and does not support about the settling failure, keeps the causal hypotheses explicitly open, and reports any numeric result only as the bounded local single-state comparison it is.
Stop if progress would require closed-loop counterfactual replay, backend execution, or non-retained warm plans/iteration traces.

Stop when the read allowance (2 evidence turns) is used or when the single authorized saved-state check is spent; do not exceed the frozen numerical budget (local_solves 6, prediction_evaluations 24) or the authorized 0.01 s horizon and 0.002 s integration step.

Do not conclude a dominant cause: a 0.01 s projected-model probe and single-execution comparisons cannot establish one, and the retained limitations state that single execution and model comparisons do not establish a dominant cause.
